name: Alphabet Inc. (Google LLC)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Google is the hyperscaler most structurally invested in storage-anchored energy: it bought a renewables developer outright (Intersect Power, ~$4.75B — 2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS, closed March 2026), anchored the largest battery project ever announced by energy capacity (300 MW / 30 GWh Form Energy iron-air, Minnesota), and signed the largest US solar+storage PPA (Steel River, up to 2.5 GW solar + 2.9 GWh BESS) — while its TPU v7 (Ironwood) became the first credible external threat to NVIDIA (Anthropic up to ~1M TPUs; Meta a multi-billion TPU lessee). BACKGROUND: Founded 1998; Alphabet holding structure since 2015. FY2025 revenue $402.8B (+15%), net income $132.2B; Google Cloud accelerated to +82% in Q2 2026 ($24.8B, backlog $514B); 2026 capex guided $195–205B after three raises; Gemini 3 launched November 2025 (app at 950M MAU); Apple selected Gemini to power the revamped Siri.
ecosystemRole: We assess Google as the ecosystem's most storage-forward buyer and its most vertically integrated: the Intersect acquisition brings development in-house ('energy parks' co-locating data centers with behind-the-meter solar+BESS to bypass interconnection queues — first: Haskell County TX, 640 MW solar + 1.3 GWh BESS beside a new campus), 1 GW of data-center demand response is signed across five utilities, and the Form Energy deal legitimizes multi-day (100-hour) storage for AI load. Its 24/7 CFE goal (66% hourly matched; footprint nonetheless +81% vs 2019) is the structural driver of all of it.

productsAndServices.name: Google Cloud & TPU Silicon
productsAndServices.category: Cloud + custom silicon · the accelerating franchise
productsAndServices.description: Google Cloud: $24.8B in Q2 2026 (+82%, fastest of the big three), $8.8B operating income, backlog $514B (nearly doubled sequentially in Q1). TPU line: v6 Trillium → v7 Ironwood (4.6 PFLOPS FP8/chip, 192 GB HBM3e, 9,216-chip pods at 42.5 exaFLOPS; GA November 2025) — now sold to select external customers rather than cloud-rental only, with Anthropic as anchor (up to ~1M TPUs) and Meta signed as a multi-year, multi-billion-dollar TPU lessee (Feb 2026). Axion Arm CPUs; Gemini 3/3.5 models; DeepMind research arm.
highlights: SemiAnalysis called Ironwood 'the 900lb gorilla' — Google's first credible merchant-silicon threat to NVIDIA; reported (not guided) internal goal of capturing ~10% of NVIDIA-class revenue
Q2 2026 headline EPS $9.11 was almost entirely mark-to-market gains on equity stakes (reported to include Anthropic and SpaceX); ex-gains ~$2.85 — roughly in line
Apple chose Gemini for the revamped Siri (2026) — distribution the antitrust remedies were designed to constrain
Cloud growth outpaced Azure (+40%) and AWS (+28%) in Q1 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The TPU vertical-integration cost edge is the analyst consensus differentiator vs NVIDIA-dependent rivals; the search-antitrust remedies (no Chrome divestiture, but exclusive-deal bans and data-sharing; DOJ cross-appeal pending) are the open regulatory overhang
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cloud consumption; TPU external sales/leases to select customers; ads auction for the core business
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Enterprises, frontier labs (Anthropic), Meta, consumers (Gemini app 950M MAU)
productsAndServices.roadmap: TPU v8 training/inference split ('Sunfish'/'Zebrafish') reported for ~2027 — not company-confirmed; 2027 capex guided to 'significantly increase' again

productsAndServices.name: Energy Parks & Storage Procurement
productsAndServices.category: Power · the most BESS-relevant hyperscaler program
productsAndServices.description: Intersect Power owned outright (~$4.75B; ~2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS operating/under construction; energy-park model co-locating DCs with behind-the-meter generation+storage — first park at Haskell County, TX: 640 MW solar + 1.3 GWh BESS). Form Energy iron-air multi-day storage: 300 MW / 30 GWh with Xcel serving the Pine Island, MN data center (largest battery project by energy capacity announced worldwide; Google pays full costs via a new tariff + $50M into Xcel's distributed-battery program). Steel River (Cypress Creek, AR): VPPA for 100% of initial output — phase 1: 1.6 GW solar + ~2 GWh BESS, full build 2.5 GW/2.9 GWh, the largest US solar+storage project to break ground. Texas: 6,200+ MW of PPAs incl. co-located solar+BESS at the Haskell DC. Demand response: 1 GW signed across I&M, TVA, Entergy Arkansas, Minnesota Power, DTE. Nuclear: Kairos master agreement (up to 500 MW; Hermes 2 groundbreaking April 2026, ops ~2030 — nothing flows before ~2030). Fusion: Commonwealth Fusion Systems 200 MW offtake (early 2030s). Hydro: Brookfield framework up to 3 GW (670 MW/$3B+ initial). Geothermal: Fervo EGS operating since 2024.
highlights: The only hyperscaler that owns a major renewables developer — vertical integration into generation+storage development itself
24/7 CFE reality check: 66% hourly matched, 12+ GW contracted in 2025 alone — but total carbon footprint +18% in 2025 and +81% vs 2019; Google concedes the moonshot is 'getting harder'
The Fort Wayne I&M deal (Clean Capacity Arrangement + ML-workload-shifting demand response) is filed as a model tariff structure for AI load
productsAndServices.positioning: Where Amazon buys storage through developer PPAs and Microsoft buys grid firmness, Google builds and owns the storage-anchored infrastructure — the deepest direct BESS demand signal in the covered set
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owned development (Intersect), VPPAs, utility tariffs, DR programs
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Counterparties: utilities (Xcel, TVA, I&M), developers (Cypress Creek), storage innovators (Form Energy, Energy Dome)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Haskell energy park completing ~2026; Steel River phases through decade-end; Hermes 2 ~2030; CFS fusion early 2030s

Funding shifted to capital markets: $24.8B notes (Nov 2025), ~$49.6B equity/convertible raise + $20.3B notes (2026)
AI-search cannibalization is the standing bear question; Google's counter: AI features drive query growth

recentDevelopments.headline: Q2 2026: revenue $119.8B (+24%) beat; Cloud +82%; capex raised a third time to $195–205B — stock fell up to ~7%
recentDevelopments.read: The Alphabet version of the sector pattern: fundamentals beat, capex shocks — with the added wrinkle that headline EPS was mostly unrealized equity gains (composition disputed across outlets; verify in the 10-Q).

recentDevelopments.headline: Steel River VPPA (Cypress Creek, Arkansas): 100% of initial output — 1.6 GW solar + ~2 GWh BESS phase 1, 2.5 GW/2.9 GWh full build
recentDevelopments.read: The largest US solar+storage PPA — and evidence that hyperscaler 24/7 goals have made BESS a core reliability asset in PPA structures. An LGES ~2.9 GWh supply role is reported but unconfirmed.

recentDevelopments.headline: $920M/month SpaceX-xAI compute deal: ~110,000 NVIDIA GPUs at xAI data centers, October 2026 through June 2029 (~$30B)
recentDevelopments.read: A frontier-lab competitor becomes a compute supplier — bridge capacity for Gemini Enterprise demand, with termination rights if GPUs slip past September 2026.

recentDevelopments.headline: Intersect Power acquisition closed (~$4.75B): ~2.2 GW solar + 2.4 GWh BESS and the energy-park development model brought in-house
recentDevelopments.read: The first Big Tech acquisition of a major renewables developer — Google now competes with the developers other hyperscalers buy from; initial focus California and Texas solar+storage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Revealed as end user of the ~700 MW Hermantown, MN data center Mortenson's development arm is entitling
recentDevelopments.read: A new siting channel: hyperscale capacity originated by a GC's land-development arm, pending an updated environmental review.

recentDevelopments.headline: 1 GW of data-center demand response signed across five US utilities; ML workloads shift off-peak
recentDevelopments.read: Google is making flexible AI load a grid asset — demand response at this scale substitutes for peaker capacity and competes with (while also complementing) storage.

recentDevelopments.headline: Pine Island, MN data center powered via Xcel: 1,400 MW wind + 200 MW solar + 300 MW/30 GWh Form Energy iron-air battery — the largest battery project by energy capacity announced anywhere
recentDevelopments.read: Multi-day (100-hour) storage enters hyperscale procurement — a category-defining deal for LDES and a template (Google pays full costs via a dedicated tariff).

recentDevelopments.headline: FY2025: revenue $402.8B, net income $132.2B; 2026 capex guided $175–185B (~doubling) — stock fell ~3% on the number
recentDevelopments.read: The original 2026 capex reset, since raised twice more — Alphabet 'reset the bar for AI infrastructure spending' (CNBC).

recentDevelopments.headline: NextEra co-development framework: gigawatt-scale data-center campuses, 15 GW of new generation by 2035 (30-35 GW upside) — after the October Duane Arnold 615 MW nuclear restart under a 25-year Google PPA
recentDevelopments.read: Google is buying generation development itself, not just PPAs — the deepest energy partnership any hyperscaler holds with an IPP.

recentDevelopments.headline: Gemini 3 launched (Deep Think mode; 1501 LMArena Elo)
recentDevelopments.read: The model line whose demand pull Pichai credits for Cloud's acceleration — and the Siri win that followed extends it into Apple's installed base.

recentDevelopments.headline: $40B Texas commitment through 2027; 6,200+ MW of Texas PPAs including co-located solar+BESS at the Haskell County campus
recentDevelopments.read: The energy-park model at state scale — generation, storage, and data centers procured as one program.

recentDevelopments.headline: Search antitrust remedies: no Chrome divestiture, but exclusive-distribution bans (incl. Gemini) and mandated data-sharing; DOJ + 38 states cross-appealed (Feb 2026)
recentDevelopments.read: Better than the worst case, unresolved into 2027 — data-sharing remedies already bind while the appeal runs.

recentDevelopments.headline: TeraWulf backstops rise to $3.2B as Fluidstack's Lake Mariner leases expand — Google warrants reach ~14% of TeraWulf pro forma
recentDevelopments.read: Google is underwriting AI-buildout credit: downside protection via lease backstops, upside via penny warrants — ~$4.5B of support across the Fluidstack chain.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Google has chosen ownership over procurement in energy: buying Intersect Power, co-developing energy parks, and anchoring first-of-kind storage (iron-air 30 GWh) and fusion offtakes make it the hyperscaler most likely to shape — rather than just consume — the storage market. Basis: closed acquisition, first-party project announcements.

(High confidence) We assess the TPU program has crossed from internal cost lever to competitive weapon: external sales, the Anthropic ~1M-TPU anchor, and Meta as a lessee give Google the only at-scale merchant alternative to NVIDIA among hyperscalers — with reported ambitions (~10% of NVIDIA-class revenue; 4.3M→35M unit projections) that remain analyst/reported figures, not guidance.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the interconnection queue is the strategic enemy Google is engineering around: energy parks (behind-the-meter generation+storage), 1 GW of demand response, and model tariff structures (Fort Wayne) all exist to add load without waiting for the grid — the playbook rivals will copy.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the sustainability gap is now structural: 66% hourly CFE but emissions +81% vs the 2019 baseline and 'moonshot getting harder' concessions — nuclear (nothing before ~2030) and fusion (early 2030s) cannot close it this decade, which keeps Google buying storage and renewables at maximum pace.

(Moderate confidence) We assess funding has shifted decisively to capital markets (~$95B of debt/equity raised across late 2025–2026) with FCF negative — sustainable at Alphabet's earnings power, but it makes the capex program hostage to equity-market patience in a way it wasn't in 2024.

(Low confidence) The Q2 2026 equity-gain composition (reported Anthropic/SpaceX marks; $37.7B vs $99B figures conflict across outlets) and Meta's reported outright TPU purchases from 2027 are unverified — treat both as unresolved.

relationships.note: Co-developing gigawatt-scale data-center campuses — 15 GW by 2035 base case — plus the Duane Arnold nuclear restart under a 25-year PPA.
relationships.context: December 2025: Google and NextEra agreed to co-develop gigawatt-scale campuses (first three in development; 15 GW of new generation for data-center hubs by 2035, 30-35 GW upside), with a technology leg putting Google Cloud AI into NextEra's grid software. It followed October's Duane Arnold deal — the 615 MW Iowa nuclear plant restarting Q1 2029 under a 25-year Google PPA. The deepest hyperscaler-IPP energy partnership on record.

relationships.note: $920M/month for ~110,000 NVIDIA GPUs at xAI data centers (Oct 2026 - Jun 2029, ~$30B).
relationships.context: Announced June 5, 2026: Google buys bridge capacity for Gemini Enterprise demand from SpaceX-xAI — ramp at reduced fees through September 2026, termination right if GPUs slip past end-September (one-month grace), and mutual 90-day cancellation after December 2026. A frontier-lab rival as compute landlord — the starkest sign that capacity scarcity outranks competitive hygiene.

relationships.note: ~$4.5B of credit backstops across the Fluidstack-TeraWulf lease chain — bought with warrants now ~14% of TeraWulf.
relationships.context: Google provides amortizing lease backstops behind Fluidstack's TeraWulf capacity ($3.2B at Lake Mariner, $1.3B at the Abernathy JV), obliged by SEC-filed mechanics to assume the leases on Fluidstack default — and took warrants equal to ~14% of TeraWulf pro forma. Downside protection plus penny-warrant upside: how AI-buildout credit actually gets underwritten.

relationships.note: GC of the ~$2B Fort Wayne campus and the New Albany 'Mustang Project'.
relationships.context: Holder is the confirmed GC of Google's ~$2B, 700+ acre Fort Wayne, Indiana data center (ground broken April 2024) and holds the OSHA-documented 'Mustang Project' in New Albany, Ohio — the low-profile incumbent of Google's hyperscale build program, with 60-70% of its projects in data centers.

relationships.note: End user of the ~700 MW Hermantown, MN site Mortenson Properties is entitling.
relationships.context: March 2026: the city of Hermantown revealed Google as end user of the ~700 MW data center Mortenson's development arm is entitling — hyperscale capacity originated through a GC's land-development channel, pending an updated environmental review with the MCEA lawsuit on hold.

relationships.note: Honeysuckle solar (188 MW, Indiana) contracted — 'supporting Google's Fort Wayne data center campus'.
relationships.context: Lightsource bp's Honeysuckle project delivers 188 MW of Indiana solar under a Google offtake explicitly framed as supporting the Fort Wayne data-center campus — PPA-mediated energy supply attached to the same campus Holder builds.

relationships.note: Reuters-reported capacity supply to Google Cloud — never company-confirmed.
relationships.context: June 2025 Reuters reporting had CoreWeave providing compute capacity to Google Cloud (which in turn supplies OpenAI); earlier reports had Google in talks to rent Blackwell GPUs. Neither company has confirmed — held as reported-only.

relationships.note: Reported Google Cloud compute supply to OpenAI after exclusivity ended — terms unconfirmed; also the defining model rival.
relationships.context: Reuters reported (June 2025) OpenAI adding Google Cloud as a compute provider, and the April 2026 Microsoft restructuring formally freed OpenAI to buy Google capacity — no primary announcement or terms. Simultaneously Gemini's chief rival: supplier economics and existential competition in one relationship.
